passages.summary: MVDs are subsets of the IFC schema created for data exchange between software; each is a standard in its own right.

An MVD defines what data must be present, what must be excluded, how entities are structured and related, and how concepts such as classification and material assignment are applied. An MVD is a standard for a specific use-case.

passages.locator: MVDs Can and Frequently Do Deviate From IFC
passages.summary: The Reference View narrows IFC's flexibility: it may allow only layer sets for materials and restrict geometry to swept solids or BReps.

passages.locator: The Danger of Unmanaged MVD Proliferation
passages.summary: IFC4precast is not interoperable with the IFC4 Reference View although both use the IFC4 schema; precast data is exchanged as .ifcprecast. Some tools have multiple IFC exports, one per MVD.

End users' information requirements (elements, properties, relationships, classification) are described with IDS; the MVD concerns the technical encoding that software must implement. The IFC2x3 Coordination View defined in-scope and out-of-scope entities.

passages.locator: Row: IFC4 ADD2 TC1 Reference View (Final, RV 1.2)
passages.summary: Simplified geometric and relational representation of spatial and physical components, to reference model information for design coordination between architectural, structural and building services domains.

passages.locator: Row: IFC4 ADD2 TC1 Design Transfer View (Draft, DTV 1.1)
passages.summary: Advanced geometric and relational representation to transfer model information from one tool to another; not a round-trip, but a higher-fidelity one-way transfer of data and responsibility. Status is Draft.

passages.locator: Row: IFC2x3 TC1 Coordination View (Final, CV 2.0)
passages.summary: Spatial and physical components for design coordination between architectural, structural and building services domains.

passages.locator: Row: IFC2x3 TC1 Basic FM Handover View (Final)
passages.summary: Handover of model information from design, construction and commissioning applications to CAFM and CMMS applications.
Needs to be exchanged as .ifcprecast due to incompatibility with the IFC4 Reference View.
Update of the IFC4 Reference View for use with IFC4.3.

sources.title: Information management according to BS EN ISO 19650. Guidance Part 2: Processes for Project Delivery

passages.locator: 5.2 Purposes of the BIM execution plan (p.82)
passages.summary: The BEP is (1) evidence to the appointing party that the delivery team can manage information to the requirements, and (2) the delivery tool the team uses to produce, manage and exchange project information during the appointment.

passages.locator: 5.3.3 Contents of the (pre-appointment) BEP, items A-G (pp.84-85)
passages.summary: ISO 19650-2 clause 5.3.2 recommends seven considerations: A individuals undertaking the information management function; B information delivery strategy; C federation strategy; D high-level responsibility matrix; E adds/amends to information production methods and procedures; F adds/amends to the information standard; G schedule of software, hardware and IT infrastructure.

A schedule listing software versions, hardware and IT to be used by the delivery team; important to enable collaboration between task teams, delivery teams and the appointing party; a fundamental consideration for wider interoperability.
ISO 19650-2 clause 5.3.2 uses 'shall consider' for the pre-appointment BEP, whereas clause 5.4.1 uses 'shall' for the BEP in the appointment.
Keep the delivery team BEP up to date throughout the appointment using change management processes.
Each appointed party produces a task information delivery plan (TIDP); the lead appointed party compiles the TIDPs into a master information delivery plan (MIDP).

Per ISO 19650-2 clause 5.4.4 the TIDP schedules the agreed information containers, identifying for each: name and title, predecessors or dependencies, level of information need, estimated production time, author, delivery milestones.
A milestone could be based on the purpose for issue, such as for comment with status S3 or published within stage 4 with status A4.

sources.title: Information management according to BS EN ISO 19650. Guidance Part B: Open data, buildingSMART and COBie

passages.summary: An MVD is a buildingSMART-sanctioned implementation of the IFC schema to satisfy a specific purpose; the IFC coordination view could support spatial coordination by reducing larger models to the relevant information.
Requirements for information exchange within the project information standard could reference MVDs.
The detailed responsibility matrix could use classes, property sets and properties within the IFC schema and the bSDD.
Quality assurance checks can be partly automated through rule-based checking that tests information against the relevant MVDs.
Properties required by an information requirement could be linked to bSDD properties to prevent ambiguity about naming or data type.

sources.title: IFC4 ADD2 TC1, 4.2.2.1 Property Sets for Objects

passages.summary: An object occurrence can be related to one or more property sets; a property set contains one or more properties. Property sets can also be related to an object type, defining common properties for all occurrences; a property on the occurrence overrides the same-named property on the type.

Default units are declared once for the whole data set and apply to all geometry, measure attributes, and properties and quantities with no local unit. Defined as SI units, conversion-based units (e.g. inch, foot with a factor to metre), derived units, or a monetary unit.

A site may carry a single geographic reference point (WGS84 longitude, latitude, elevation) establishing where the 0,0,0 of the site local placement sits in the real world. The site placement is relative to the world coordinate system established by the project representation context, which may define true north.

IfcClassification identifies the classification system a classification reference refers to; examples of formally published systems are Omniclass, Uniclass, Masterformat, DIN277. A system may be included in full or referenced by key/id through IfcClassificationReference.

sources.title: IFC4 ADD2 TC1, 4.1.4 Project Global Positioning

passages.summary: New in IFC4: a geospatial coordinate reference system on the geometric representation context positions the project coordinate system on earth, normally using eastings, northings, elevation above datum and orientation.

sources.title: Information management according to BS EN ISO 19650. Guidance Part 1: Concepts

passages.summary: The federation strategy is a higher-level description of how and why the information model is divided up via the information container breakdown structure. Together they provide the rules for combining and segregating containers for purposes such as security, spatial coordination or information transmission.

The lead appointed party confirms the federation strategy for the delivery team in the BEP; the appointing party may set it project-wide in the information production methods and procedures. Both should be communicated to all delivery team members and may evolve during the appointment.
